Hi Asha — answering each of your clarifying points below. I kept this email threaded to make it easy to paste into your spreadsheet; the attached attestation template is what we deliver after a completed erase. Happy to walk through any item on the call (we confirmed Thu 09:30 PT with procurement).

1) Backups & snapshots
- Storage location: Full backups and snapshots for hosted accounts are stored in the same primary cloud region selected for the account by default (e.g., us-east-1 for Acme). We do not cross-replicate backups to another geographic region except for disaster recovery scenarios where the customer has explicitly agreed to cross-region DR in their subscription.
- Retention: Backups are retained for 90 days by default.
- Deletion SLA: When a deletion request for a tenant is approved, primary store deletion begins immediately; backups and snapshots are purged on a rolling schedule and completed within 45 calendar days. We provide a deletion ticket with timestamps of each purge step.

2) Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) / KMS
- Redwood supports customer-managed keys for enterprise-hosted plans via our KMS integration (AWS KMS / GCP KMS). For standard hosted accounts we use Redwood-managed keys.
- BYOK effect on deletion: If Acme chooses BYOK, key revocation renders stored ciphertext unrecoverable, providing a cryptographic means of data destruction. We combine key-revocation with logical deletion for full assurance; note that cryptographic destruction is an option we coordinate during onboarding and is not the default for self-service signups.

3) Evidence & attestation
- We provide a deletion attestation PDF that includes: ticket id, tenant id, objects deleted, timestamps for primary and backup deletions, and operator signature. Standard turnaround: attestation issued within 5 business days after purge completion.
- Audit trail: all delete operations are logged in our internal audit log (immutable append-only entries) and a sanitized copy (no raw PII) can be shared under an NDA for audit purposes. Audit logs are retained per contract (standard: 365 days for enterprise customers).

4) Edge / ephemeral caches
- Edge caches and KV prefix caches are short-lived by design. By default:
  • In-memory inference caches: TTL <= 60 seconds for low-latency variants.
  • Persistent prefix/KV caches used for performance are stored encrypted and have configurable TTLs; default retention is 7 days but can be set to shorter windows for enterprise accounts.
- PII: we recommend customers avoid sending sensitive PII in prompts where possible. If PII is present, it will reside only following the configured retention windows above and is covered by our encryption and access controls.

Additional notes and contractual options
- Default hosted retention: Redwood stores request/response payloads for 30 days for operational/debug/billing purposes. Customers can opt into a reduced retention (30d -> 0d) or enterprise retention exhibits that set explicit retention windows and backup handling.
- Fast erase add-on: for customers who require compressed deletion windows, we offer a paid ‘fast erase’ SLA that guarantees backup purge within 15 calendar days and expedited attestation delivery.
- Data residency exhibit: we will include a contract exhibit that codifies primary region, backup policy, and the deletion SLA you select.

Deliverables I will attach to the ticket after our call:
- Completed in-line questionnaire (spreadsheet) with per-field answers.
- Redwood_Deletion_Attestation_Template.pdf (attached)
- Link to support ticket where the delete request will be tracked: https://support.redwood.ai/ticket/98765

Security controls summary (brief)
- Encryption: TLS in transit; AES-256 at rest.
- Access controls: RBAC and least-privilege; production environments require multi-person approval for manual deletion operations.
- Certifications: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II (scope: hosted inference, logging, and billing subsystems) — we can provide the report under NDA.
